assessment: This ETL supports a bounded host-path conclusion for this single C# HidD_GetInputReport call: it failed with Win32 error 1, and no corresponding GET_REPORT setup reached the observed UCX/xHCI stack. Complete target setup fields, zero reported ETW event/buffer loss, a successful GET_DESCRIPTOR in-window, and subsequent healthy CDC control/bulk traffic strengthen that inference. It does not establish physical-wire absence, identify the exact rejecting Windows component, explain the earlier native IOCTL, or validate device-side GET_REPORT handling or real interrupt/input behavior.

evidence.etl: usb.etl; 5006 events; target pointer 0x20f265a47398; VID_239A/PID_CAFE; strict and -lr setup signatures agree; both report zero lost events/buffers
evidence.target_setup: 40 target setup events (20 dispatch and 20 completion), all setup fields present; all control completions successful; no bmRequestType=A1/bRequest=01 GET_REPORT
evidence.query: One C# HidD_GetInputReport on matching COL02, length 6, 2026-10-04T12:13:54.6815162Z through 12:13:54.7131570Z; FALSE, Win32 error 1; hex=null; failed_buffer_hex is not device data
evidence.positive_controls: Successful GET_DESCRIPTOR string request in the query interval; subsequent target CDC control and bulk traffic succeeds
evidence.cancellations: Two endpoint rundown-mapped cancellations are CDC endpoints 0x82 and 0x81, length 0, near CDC close; neither is HID endpoint 0x83/0x84
evidence.time: XML SystemTime carries anomalous +07:59 offset; timestamps were aligned to raw TraceHeader UTC anchor 2026-10-04T12:13:54.238720Z plus relative time, not parsed using that offset

limitations: ETW observes the Windows USB software stack, not a physical USB analyzer; absence is bounded to the enabled UCX/xHCI trace boundary.
This applies only to the C# HidD_GetInputReport call, not the earlier native DeviceIoControl attempt.
No firmware GET_REPORT callback, interrupt input payload, physical key/mouse movement, XY/Y behavior, or game behavior was validated.
Strict XML localized EventID 4 labels are not trusted; the manifest/-lr identifies device rundown.
